@shadcn sorry for the unexpected PR but I think this small change will reduce warnings and make the library more future proof.

This PR will resolve a lot of proxy-related issues I am having with `NO_PROXY=` support in shadcn/ui too.

Great stuff!
I've added this to the roadmap. I'll start looking into this now. Thanks for the great work @nbouvrette This is already looking good.

@shadcn merged `main` in and resolved the conflicts — this is green again.

Since #10905 landed the `undici` swap and the `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` handling from the original version of this PR, I've **rescoped this branch to just the remaining delta: SOCKS and PAC.** Net diff is now +815/−33 across 7 files, down from the original ~854 lines touching the whole fetch stack. Title and description are updated to match.

On the conflict resolution, since `proxy.ts` came back as an add/add:

- **`fetchWithProxy`, `fetchOnce` and `getFailureReason` are preserved verbatim**, including the cross-origin redirect hardening from #11196 and its 5 tests. I took your `fetcher.ts` wholesale.
- The **only** line removed from your version is the module-level `EnvHttpProxyAgent` const, replaced by `createProxyDispatcher(env)`. That factory gates HTTP/HTTPS on the identical four env vars and returns the identical `EnvHttpProxyAgent`, so it's a strict superset — it just checks PAC and SOCKS ahead of it. `git diff` against `main` confirms those 10 lines are the whole removal.
- `proxy.test.ts` is the union of both suites; they cover different exports (`createProxyDispatcher` vs `fetchWithProxy`) with no overlap.
- Lockfile was regenerated from `main`'s so the diff contains only `socks`, `pac-resolver`, `quickjs-wasi` and their transitives.

`pnpm typecheck` is clean and all 1720 tests across 83 files pass.

Two things worth a look when you review:

1. **`quickjs-wasi` is ~3 MB on disk.** It's there so PAC scripts — arbitrary JavaScript fetched over the network — run in a WASM sandbox rather than the CLI's own runtime. If you'd rather not take that weight, I'm happy to split PAC into a separate PR and land SOCKS on its own; SOCKS only needs `socks` (~50 KB) and covers the more common case.
2. **`ALL_PROXY` only activates the SOCKS branch for `socks*://` schemes**, per the curl convention. `ALL_PROXY=http://…` is deliberately left to the explicit `HTTP_PROXY` variable rather than being silently absorbed — happy to change that if you'd prefer it to be permissive.

@axieum the `NO_PROXY` support you asked about shipped in #10905, so that should be working for you on latest already.

@pomeh thanks again for the review earlier — the integration tests you pushed for are still in here and now cover the SOCKS and PAC paths against real local servers.

@nbouvrette Good call on splitting it up. Let's rescope this PR to SOCKS only and move PAC to a follow-up. And keep ALL_PROXY as socks-only. Thanks for working on this. Appreciate it.

(Let's also bump changeset to minor while we're at it).

Done — rescoped to SOCKS only. PAC is out of this branch entirely and will come as a follow-up PR once this lands; the work is parked on a branch so nothing's lost.

- **PAC removed**: `PacDispatcher`, the directive parser, `PAC_URL` handling and the `pac-resolver` type stub are gone, along with the `pac-resolver` and `quickjs-wasi` dependencies. That's the ~3 MB of WASM off the dependency tree — `socks` (~50 KB) is now the only addition.
- **`ALL_PROXY` stays SOCKS-only**, as you asked — a non-`socks*` scheme falls through to the explicit `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` variables rather than being silently absorbed. There's a unit test and an integration test pinning that behavior.
- **Changeset bumped to `minor`.**

Net diff is now **+485/−32 across 6 files**, down from +815/−33 across 7. The lockfile diff is 32 lines and is entirely socks-driven: `socks` was already in there as a transitive of `socks-proxy-agent` at 2.8.6, so promoting it to a direct dep moves it to 2.8.9 and updates its `ip-address` dep. Regenerated with the repo's pinned pnpm 10.33.4 and verified with `--frozen-lockfile`.

`fetchWithProxy`/`fetchOnce`/`getFailureReason` are byte-identical to `main` apart from one explanatory comment, so the cross-origin redirect hardening from #11196 is untouched. `pnpm typecheck` is clean and all 1711 tests across 83 files pass.

Title and description are updated to match. The only red check is the Vercel preview, which needs a shadcn-pro member to authorize the deploy from my fork.
@shadcn tagging you just in case - let me know if anything needs adjusting! 🙏

Rescope looks great. Thanks @nbouvrette 

Once CI is green. I'll merge this.
